label: <DEL> delimiter step in length-4 sequences
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at the <DEL> delimiter step (t = L, recall_idx 0) of sequences with exactly 4 original tokens; it is active on ~99% of such steps. It never fires during the original or copy phases, and only negligibly at the delimiter of L=3 or L=5 sequences (tiny activations, about 0.1% of mass); it is silent for L >= 6. Magnitude is modulated by the content of the 4 tokens: when the last original token equals the first (e.g. z y o z), mean activation is about 1.5x the average, and when two adjacent original tokens repeat (e.g. l x x l), it is about 0.65x the average. More digits among the originals also lowers the firing rate. The rare inactive L=4 delimiters mostly have adjacent repeated tokens.

issues: Core predicate holds on the test split: P 0.990, R 0.991, F1 0.990, mass recall 0.999. In the profile, all activation is at the delimiter (original and copy phases are 0.000), with 99.9% of the mass at L=4.
The missed activations (689) are weak delimiter firings at L=3 (about 4% of L=3 delimiters, 0.1% of mass) and L=5 (tiny). This matches the explanation and is not a missing class.

Magnitude claims hold up. Adjacent-repeat L=4 delimiters carry 5.7% of the mass but 8.9% of the active steps, so about 0.64x the mean (claimed 0.65x). orig(3)==orig(0) carries 4.9% of the mass and 3.3% of active steps, so about 1.46x (claimed 1.5x).

Inactive L=4 delimiters: about 490 of the 698 false positives have adjacent repeats (precision 0.93 in that subset vs 0.997 without them), so 'mostly adjacent repeats' holds. The digit effect is real but small (precision 0.982 with n_digits>=2 vs 0.990 with no digits). 'Lowers the firing rate' is accurate but slightly overstated in emphasis.
